# THERM product sync — display precision (2026-09-24)

## Discussion
- The pilot customer informally asked whether the device screen could show two decimals instead of one (MRD-02).
- Firmware: formatting 0.01 steps is easy; SW-22b is still written for one decimal.
- Hardware: resolution target is 0.05 °C and accuracy ±0.1 °C, so a second decimal shows digits we cannot stand behind.
- QA: a change would need new TC-D-06 expected values and a rerun; TC-D-06 is one of the six DVT bars.

## Outcome
- No decision. Nothing changes before the customer review on 2026-09-30.

## Actions
- Mara Lindqvist: add display precision to the 2026-09-30 customer review agenda.

Mara Lindqvist: Informally. Their nurses asked whether the screen could show two decimals instead of one.

# Kestrel Valley Care pilot review — MRD-02 display (2026-09-30)

## Decision
- APPROVED by Mara Lindqvist (Product lead): MRD-02 display changes from one decimal to two decimals (0.01 °C), at Kestrel Valley Care's request. The ±0.1 °C accuracy requirement is unchanged.

## Why
- Kestrel Valley Care's nurses compare readings with a reference that shows two decimals; one decimal causes repeated re-checks.
- The second decimal is display resolution only.

## Actions
- {{TEST_PERSON}}: update MRD-02 and the PRD display requirement (PRD-D01), due 2026-10-07.
- Jonas Becker: update SW-22b number formatting, due 2026-10-09.
- Rafael Moreno: update TC-D-06 expected results and plan the rerun, due 2026-10-09.
transcript: {{TEST_PERSON}}: Thanks for joining. The main item today is how the reading shows on the device screen.
Ines Varga: Our nurses log readings next to a reference unit that shows two decimals. With one decimal they keep re-checking and writing notes.
Mara Lindqvist: So the ask is a two-decimal display, 0.01 degree steps, on the device.

Jonas Becker: Formatting is easy. I want to be clear that accuracy is still plus or minus 0.1 degrees. The extra digit is display resolution, not accuracy.
Ines Varga: Understood. We need the screen to match the reference sheet, not a new accuracy claim.
Rafael Moreno: Then TC-D-06 has to change. Today it checks the displayed value against a one-decimal rounding rule.

{{TEST_PERSON}}: Recording that as approved by Mara today, September 30.
{{TEST_PERSON}}: I'll update MRD-02 and the PRD display requirement by October 7.
Jonas Becker: I'll change the SW-22b formatting. October 9 works for me.
Rafael Moreno: I'll update the TC-D-06 expected results and plan the rerun, also by October 9.
Ines Varga: Will this delay the pilot?
{{TEST_PERSON}}: Not on its own. The DVT hold is about accuracy, not the display.
Mara Lindqvist: We'll confirm the pilot timing once the DVT dates settle.
Ines Varga: That works. Thank you.

# BUG-412 failure review (2026-10-05)

## Decisions
- Likely cause of BUG-412: sensor self-heating under load (backlight and radio on). Filter dropout (SW-14c) deprioritized, not ruled out. Not a confirmed root cause.
- Hardware owns the BUG-412 fix (HW-11 board layout); Firmware supports with sample-accounting logs.
- TRACE-01 stays open until QA confirms the MRD-01 link and the fix owner is recorded in Jira.

## Why
- The failing TC-D-03 rerun accepted 100 of 100 samples, so dropped samples do not explain the offset.
- The offset appears only with backlight and radio on and rises over about two minutes; the regulator sits next to the sensor.

## Actions
- Tomas Okafor: propose the board thermal fix and name the candidate board revision, due 2026-10-08.
- Jonas Becker: add sample-accounting logging to the next firmware build, due 2026-10-12.
- Rafael Moreno: confirm whether TC-D-03 traces to MRD-01 and send the confirmation to {{TEST_PERSON}} for TRACE-01, due 2026-10-12.
transcript: Tomas Okafor: Goal today is a likely cause for BUG-412 and a fix owner. Not a confirmed root cause.
Jonas Becker: I reran TC-D-03 with sample-count logging. 100 of 100 samples accepted in the failing run. No dropouts.
Rafael Moreno: So the filter-dropout hypothesis in the ticket doesn't explain it.
Tomas Okafor: The offset only shows with the backlight and radio both on, and it climbs over about two minutes. That looks thermal.
Jonas Becker: Self-heating near the sensor, from the regulator under load?
Tomas Okafor: That's my read. The regulator sits right next to the sensor on the current layout.
{{TEST_PERSON}}: Are we calling that the root cause?
Tomas Okafor: No. Likely cause. We confirm it on the reworked board.
Rafael Moreno: Then keep the firmware hypothesis open, just at lower priority.
{{TEST_PERSON}}: Decision, then: the likely cause is sensor self-heating under load. Filter dropout is deprioritized, not ruled out.
Tomas Okafor: And Hardware owns the fix. It's a layout change on the HW-11 board.
Jonas Becker: Firmware will support with sample-accounting logs in the next build, by October 12.
{{TEST_PERSON}}: What about TRACE-01? It's still open.
Rafael Moreno: It stays open. I haven't confirmed that TC-D-03 traces to MRD-01, and the fix owner isn't recorded in Jira yet.
{{TEST_PERSON}}: Okay, TRACE-01 stays open. Rafael, can you send me that confirmation?
Rafael Moreno: By October 12.
Tomas Okafor: I'll propose the board fix and name the candidate revision by October 8.
{{TEST_PERSON}}: Note that DVT-R2 assumed a firmware-only change. A board change means new sample boards.
Tomas Okafor: Right. That could move the DVT-R2 date. Let's look at it once the supplier gives a delivery date.

decisions: BUG-412's likely cause is sensor self-heating under load (backlight and radio on); the firmware filter-dropout hypothesis (SW-14c) is deprioritized, not ruled out. This is not a confirmed root cause.
Hardware owns the BUG-412 fix (HW-11 board layout); Firmware supports with sample-accounting logs.
TRACE-01 stays open until QA confirms the MRD-01 link and the fix owner is recorded in Jira.
